title: November 2026: Class overviews, announcements, modules, and grading in the gradebook
summary: Flint's November 2026 updates give every class an Overview page, and add class announcements, modules, grading in the gradebook, and sending grades to your LMS.
body_markdown:
This month, every class in Flint gets a home page. You can also post announcements to a class, organize units into modules, and grade right in the gradebook. Here's what's new.


## Every class has an Overview page


Classes now open on an Overview page that shows what's due this week, announcements, pinned resources, and anything that needs your attention. Sparky also writes a daily brief at the top with a suggested next step, such as drafting a reminder about an overdue activity.


Students get their own Overview, with their overdue work first, then this week's deadlines and their progress on each.[Learn about the class Overview page](https://help.flintk12.com/articles/get-started-with-flint-for-teachers) .


## Keep your class in the loop with announcements


Post an update to the whole class from its Overview, without creating an activity. Attach up to 10 files from your device, Google Drive, or OneDrive, email the announcement to your students, or schedule it to go out later. Give an announcement like "Permission slips due Friday" an expiration date, and students stop seeing it once that day has passed.[Learn about announcements](https://help.flintk12.com/articles/get-started-with-flint-for-teachers) .


## Organize your lessons with modules


The new **Modules** tab groups a class's activities and resources into units, weeks, or whatever structure fits your class, up to three levels deep. Drag everything into teaching order and publish each module when your students are ready for it. Students only see published modules.[Learn more about modules](https://help.flintk12.com/articles/organizing-a-class-into-modules) .


## Grade right in the gradebook


Pick a rubric grade or type points straight into a gradebook cell. Mark work Missing, Late, or Excused, give every student who hasn't handed anything in the same score at once with **Fill empty cells** , and add a column for work done outside Flint, like a paper test.


Blank cells no longer count as zeros, so overall scores stay accurate while you're still grading.[Learn more about Flint's gradebook](https://help.flintk12.com/articles/everything-you-need-to-know-about-flints-gradebook) .


## Send grades to your LMS


Stop entering grades twice. Flint can send grades to Canvas, Google Classroom, or Schoology. Press **Send to LMS** in the gradebook or on an activity, and each student's newest grade goes to the matching class. Flint marks which grades arrived and which still need to go, and the next send picks up the ones that didn't.


To turn on grade sending for your school, ask your Customer Success contact or emailsupport@flintk12.com .[Learn about sending grades to your LMS](https://help.flintk12.com/articles/sending-grades-to-your-lms) .


## Discover and share resources other teachers made


Made something great with Sparky? Publish interactives, slide decks, documents, and spreadsheets to your school, your district, or the public library. The library now lists these resources beside activities, so you can browse what other teachers made, like the ones you use, and add any of them to your classes.[Learn about the library](https://help.flintk12.com/articles/activities-and-resources-in-the-library) .


## Format spreadsheets and add charts


Bold, color, and border cells, then turn a selection into a bar, line, or pie chart. You can also ask Sparky to format the spreadsheet for you. Formatting and charts carry into the Excel download, or open the spreadsheet in Google Sheets.[Learn more about spreadsheets](https://help.flintk12.com/articles/spreadsheets-in-flint) .


## Additional updates


- Students can join a class with its six-character join code.
- Every class has a Resources tab, and a new Resources page lists everything you've made.
- Students can hand in files from Google Drive and OneDrive.
- Assessments can include ordering, matching, and fill-in-the-table questions.
- Download every file students made in an activity in one go.
- Students are reminded to submit their work before they leave a chat session.
- Try any published activity as a student, even when it isn't in a class.
